comment:
* This is a utility class to add swipe to dismiss and drag & drop support to RecyclerView. *

* It works with a RecyclerView and a Callback class, which configures what type of interactions * are enabled and also receives events when user performs these actions. *

* Depending on which functionality you support, you should override * {@link Callback#onMove(RecyclerView, ViewHolder, ViewHolder)} and / or * {@link Callback#onSwiped(ViewHolder, int)}. *

* This class is designed to work with any LayoutManager but for certain situations, it can be * optimized for your custom LayoutManager by extending methods in the * {@link ItemTouchHelper.Callback} class or implementing {@link ItemTouchHelper.ViewDropHandler} * interface in your LayoutManager. *

* By default, ItemTouchHelper moves the items' translateX/Y properties to reposition them. On * platforms older than Honeycomb, ItemTouchHelper uses canvas translations and View's visibility * property to move items in response to touch events. You can customize these behaviors by * overriding {@link Callback#onChildDraw(Canvas, RecyclerView, ViewHolder, float, float, int, * boolean)} * or {@link Callback#onChildDrawOver(Canvas, RecyclerView, ViewHolder, float, float, int, * boolean)}. *

* Most of the time, you only need to override onChildDraw but due to limitations of * platform prior to Honeycomb, you may need to implement onChildDrawOver as well.

variables.name: UP
variables.comment: * Up direction, used for swipe & drag control.

variables.name: DOWN
variables.comment: * Down direction, used for swipe & drag control.

variables.name: LEFT
variables.comment: * Left direction, used for swipe & drag control.

variables.name: RIGHT
variables.comment: * Right direction, used for swipe & drag control.

variables.name: START
variables.comment:
* Horizontal start direction. Resolved to LEFT or RIGHT depending on RecyclerView's layout
     * direction. Used for swipe & drag control.

variables.name: END
variables.comment:
* Horizontal end direction. Resolved to LEFT or RIGHT depending on RecyclerView's layout
     * direction. Used for swipe & drag control.

variables.name: ACTION_STATE_IDLE
variables.comment:
* ItemTouchHelper is in idle state. At this state, either there is no related motion event by
     * the user or latest motion events have not yet triggered a swipe or drag.

variables.name: ACTION_STATE_SWIPE
variables.comment: * A View is currently being swiped.

variables.name: ACTION_STATE_DRAG
variables.comment: * A View is currently being dragged.

variables.name: ANIMATION_TYPE_SWIPE_SUCCESS
variables.comment: * Animation type for views which are swiped successfully.

variables.name: ANIMATION_TYPE_SWIPE_CANCEL
variables.comment:
* Animation type for views which are not completely swiped thus will animate back to their
     * original position.

variables.name: ANIMATION_TYPE_DRAG
variables.comment: * Animation type for views that were dragged and now will animate to their final position.

variables.name: PIXELS_PER_SECOND
variables.comment: * The unit we are using to track velocity

variables.name: mPendingCleanup
variables.comment:
* Views, whose state should be cleared after they are detached from RecyclerView.
     * This is necessary after swipe dismissing an item. We wait until animator finishes its job
     * to clean these views.

variables.name: mTmpPosition
variables.comment: * Re-use array to calculate dx dy for a ViewHolder

variables.name: mSelected
variables.comment: * Currently selected view holder

variables.name: mInitialTouchX
variables.comment:
* The reference coordinates for the action start. For drag & drop, this is the time long
     * press is completed vs for swipe, this is the initial touch point.

variables.name: mSwipeEscapeVelocity
variables.comment: * Set when ItemTouchHelper is assigned to a RecyclerView.

variables.name: mMaxSwipeVelocity
variables.comment: * Set when ItemTouchHelper is assigned to a RecyclerView.

variables.name: mDx
variables.comment: * The diff between the last event and initial touch.

variables.name: mSelectedStartX
variables.comment:
* The coordinates of the selected view at the time it is selected. We record these values
     * when action starts so that we can consistently position it even if LayoutManager moves the
     * View.

variables.name: mActivePointerId
variables.comment: * The pointer we are tracking.

variables.name: mCallback
variables.comment: * Developer callback which controls the behavior of ItemTouchHelper.

variables.name: mActionState
variables.comment: * Current mode.

variables.name: mSelectedFlags
variables.comment:
* The direction flags obtained from unmasking
     * {@link Callback#getAbsoluteMovementFlags(RecyclerView, ViewHolder)} for the current
     * action state.

variables.name: mRecoverAnimations
variables.comment:
* When a View is dragged or swiped and needs to go back to where it was, we create a Recover
     * Animation and animate it to its location using this custom Animator, instead of using
     * framework Animators.
     * Using framework animators has the side effect of clashing with ItemAnimator, creating
     * jumpy UIs.

variables.name: mScrollRunnable
variables.comment:
* When user drags a view to the edge, we start scrolling the LayoutManager as long as View
     * is partially out of bounds.

variables.name: mVelocityTracker
variables.comment: * Used for detecting fling swipe

variables.name: mSwapTargets
variables.comment: re-used list for selecting a swap target

variables.name: mDistances
variables.comment: re used for for sorting swap targets

variables.name: mChildDrawingOrderCallback
variables.comment: * If drag & drop is supported, we use child drawing order to bring them to front.

variables.name: mOverdrawChild
variables.comment:
* This keeps a reference to the child dragged by the user. Even after user stops dragging,
     * until view reaches its final position (end of recover animation), we keep a reference so
     * that it can be drawn above other children.

variables.name: mOverdrawChildPosition
variables.comment:
* We cache the position of the overdraw child to avoid recalculating it each time child
     * position callback is called. This value is invalidated whenever a child is attached or
     * detached.

variables.name: mGestureDetector
variables.comment: * Used to detect long press.

variables.name: mTmpRect
variables.comment: * Temporary rect instance that is used when we need to lookup Item decorations.

variables.name: mDragScrollStartTimeInMs
variables.comment: * When user started to drag scroll. Reset when we don't scroll

methods.name: public void startDrag(ViewHolder viewHolder)
methods.comment:
* Starts dragging the provided ViewHolder. By default, ItemTouchHelper starts a drag when a * View is long pressed. You can disable that behavior by overriding * {@link ItemTouchHelper.Callback#isLongPressDragEnabled()}. *

* For this method to work: *

    *
  • The provided ViewHolder must be a child of the RecyclerView to which this * ItemTouchHelper * is attached.
    • *
  • {@link ItemTouchHelper.Callback} must have dragging enabled.
    • *
  • There must be a previous touch event that was reported to the ItemTouchHelper * through RecyclerView's ItemTouchListener mechanism. As long as no other ItemTouchListener * grabs previous events, this should work as expected.
    • *
* * For example, if you would like to let your user to be able to drag an Item by touching one * of its descendants, you may implement it as follows: * 
     *     viewHolder.dragButton.setOnTouchListener(new View.OnTouchListener() {
     *         public boolean onTouch(View v, MotionEvent event) {
     *             if (MotionEvent.getActionMasked(event) == MotionEvent.ACTION_DOWN) {
     *                 mItemTouchHelper.startDrag(viewHolder);
     *             }
     *             return false;
     *         }
     *     });
     *
*

* * @param viewHolder The ViewHolder to start dragging. It must be a direct child of * RecyclerView. * @see ItemTouchHelper.Callback#isItemViewSwipeEnabled()
